points.point: Standing requirement: the slice at z = 0 is the flat set (every approach except the classic Mandelbulb)
points.user_view: For Sphere inversions, Lathe, Mandelbulb and Split the 2D view at z = 0 matches a flat set I computed in Python, at powers 2, 3 and -2, in Mandelbrot mode and for the Julia constants (-1, 0) and (-0.123, 0.745). At powers 2 and 3 the pixels that disagree are 0.77 to 1.58 percent of the picture, which is the outline; none lies more than 4 pixels from it. At power -2 the page draws the fine dust a little fatter than my pixel test (0.59 to 1.28 percent disagree, some pixels 2 to 4 pixels off), which I did not get to the bottom of.

The Julia section has a drop-down "Jump to a point" with 26 ready-made points in three groups. Typing a name and pressing Save puts the point in a group "Your saved points" at the top, kept in the browser's storage; a Delete button shows only while a saved point is chosen and removes it. I did not try blocked storage, a reload, or many saved points.

Sphere inversions is the first approach in the list, and its slice at z = 0 is the flat Mandelbrot or Julia set to within the outline (0.84 percent of pixels at power 2, 9 pixels of 604,262 more than 2 pixels off, none more than 4). Checked at the approach's opening settings only (one plane, no turn, no lift).

The Mandelbrot options have a "Julia mosaic" tick box. Ticking it in 3D draws a layer of small Julia solids and opens the cut at z = 0 by itself; in the 2D view it fills the picture with a grid of flat Julia sets, which is the Wikipedia picture. At the opening camera the 3D mosaic is small, in the middle third of the picture; I looked at one picture of each, at thumbnail size.

The "2D view" tick box sits above the Show row (304 against 464 pixels from the top at 1400 x 950) and its label says which slice it shows: "2D view (slice at z = 0)". The picture it gives is the flat set, by the numbers above.

The Mandelbulb has Latitude phase and Longitude phase dials with a Sweep button, the classic Mandelbulb has its two phase dials, and Sphere inversions has Turn and Lift. Pictures drew without errors at a phase of 40 degrees and at Turn 40 with Lift 0.3. I did not press Sweep or watch the solid pulse, and took no phase-0 pictures to compare against.

All five approaches draw a solid at power -2 with no errors, and the power box shows -2. The 3D pictures are intricate, fibrous shapes that run off the top and bottom of the opening frame, because moving the power does not move the camera. Only -2 was tried; no other negative power, no fractional one, and not the typed limit.

The saved Julia points are now a drop-down like the Kleinian one: "Your own values" first, then the user's saved points, then Classic sets (18), Found by exploring (2) and Found with two planes (6). It reads "Your own values" whenever c is on no entry. The Kleinian list has the same shape with four groups, 34 entries in all.

Picking a Julia entry changed only c; camera, 2D frame, iterations, planes and Kleinian depth stayed. "Frame it" changed only the camera, and "As it was found" on Flint changed only Planes (to 2), then hid itself. Picking a Kleinian entry changed only the group and sphere values, and its "Frame it" only the camera and the 2D frame. One entry of each list was tried.

With flip z on, the slice at z = 0 gives the same numbers as without it in all 36 cases. For Sphere inversions and the Lathe, four Julia sets with c in the plane z = 0, each seen from two sides, are pixel-identical with and without flip z (largest channel difference 0 in all 16 pairs). I set flip z through the page state, with the box showing ticked, not by clicking the box.

defects.title: While the graphics context is lost the status line keeps its old text and nothing says why the picture stopped
defects.repro: Run: PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 python out/t6/walk/once.py context (parts 1 and 2).
